articles.title: Meta India head named in case over Facebook videos targeting PM Modi
articles.description: Police in the southern Indian city of Hyderabad have registered a case against the head of Meta India over multiple videos posted on the company’s Facebook platform that depicted Prime Minister Narendra Modi in an “abusive manner”, a senior police officer said on Friday. Police are preparing to send a notice to Meta Platforms regarding the case, which had not been issued as of Friday, said V Aravind Babu, deputy commissioner of police for cyber crimes in Hyderabad. Meta did not immediately respond to Reuters ’ requests for comment on Friday. The case adds to a string of tensions between Meta and Modi’s government over content tied to the prime minister. India’s IT ministry summoned Meta executives this week after Facebook briefly restricted a Modi post last week, with a top official saying the government wanted Meta to explain the matter at the highest level. A Meta spokesperson said at the time that the post, which was Modi’s first where he addressed massive student protests that forced the resignation of the education minister , had been blocked inadvertently. Modi has also come in for a barrage of online criticism, jokes and ridicule by protesters in recent weeks. India is Facebook’s biggest market by users.

articles.title: Search underway to locate 10 climbers missing after Broad Peak avalanche
articles.description: A search operation was underway on Friday to locate 10 climbers, including renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja and Pakistani climber Sohail Sakhi, who went missing on Broad Peak a day earlier after an avalanche struck around midday. The Alpine Club of Pakistan (ACP) said that the missing climbers included six Nepalese climbers, a Pakistani, an Omani, an American and a climber from China. The climbers from Nepal were identified as Purja, Pur Bahadur Gurung, Kili Pemba Sherpa, Nima Sherpa, Nawang Thindu Sherpa and Gyalu Sherpa. It identified the remaining climbers as Nadhira Ahmed Abdullah Al Harthy from Oman, Sakhi from Pakistan, Wang Zhong from China and Mallory Geis from the United States. In a statement issued on Friday, ACP Senior Vice President Karrar Haidri said two Pakistan Army Aviation rescue helicopters, carrying rescue personnel and additional specialised equipment, had been dispatched to support the ongoing search and rescue operation. The statement said ACP’s Major General Irfan Arshad, HI(M), along with the club’s senior leadership, remained in constant contact with the highest government authorities and relevant agencies to facilitate the rescue operation. “Every possible effort is being made to ensure that helicopter support and all available rescue resources are mobilised at the earliest opportunity, subject to weather and operational conditions,” it added. The club said it was closely monitoring the situation and coordinating with all relevant stakeholders while expressing solidarity with the climbers’ families and the international mountaineering community. ACP’s General Secretary Ayaz Shigri told Dawn that several expedition teams had jointly begun their summit push before the incident. He said GPS locations received from some of the missing climbers indicated that the avalanche had swept the group about 1,000 metres downhill, leaving them trapped. Shigri said helicopter-assisted rescue operations were expected to begin on Friday morning. He said there were also fears that some local high-altitude porters might have been affected by the avalanche. “We pray for the safety of all the climbers. It is a big incident,” he said. Purja, 43, who served with Britain’s Brigade of Gurkhas before joining the Special Boat Squadron of the Royal Marines, has broken multiple climbing records since becoming a full-time mountaineer and tour guide. He climbed all 14 “eight-thousanders” (peaks above 8,000 metres, or 26,000 feet) in six months and six days between April and October 2019 — then a record. In 2021, Purja completed the first winter ascent of K2 along with a team of nine other Nepalese climbers. Sakhi, who hails from Hunza, had successfully summited Kanchenjunga (8,58­6m), the world’s 3rd highest mountain, in Nepal earlier in May. He had previously scaled K2, Nanga Parbat, Gasherbrum I and Gasherbrum II without supplemental oxygen, establishing himself among the country’s strongest high-altitude climbers. Additional input from AFP

articles.title: Trump administration stops work on Great Lakes Asian carp project near Joliet
articles.description:
Gov. JB Pritzker is calling on the Trump administration to immediately reverse a work stoppage on an embattled project needed to keep invasive Asian carp out of the Great Lakes near Joliet.

Contractors at the Brandon Road Interbasin Project received a work stoppage order on July 24 stating the project is under administrative review, despite about $2 million worth of material already on site. Work was slated to begin this week, with shaft drilling scheduled for September. Jobsite trailers were also already set up at the project, according to Will County officials.

"Under my administration, Illinois has spearheaded this project to protect the entire Great Lakes region. Yet, the Trump Administration repeatedly throws up roadblocks and has now ordered work to stop altogether with no explanations,” Pritzker said Thursday. “The Great Lakes provide drinking water to more than 40 million people and support a $52 billion regional economy. It's time for the Trump Administration to uphold the federal government’s obligations, stop playing political games, and move this project forward.”

The $1.15 billion project in the Des Plaines River near Joliet is seen as a crucial way to stop invasive Asian carp from entering the Great Lakes. Without a barrier, the carp could wreak havoc on the $20 billion fishing and boating industries and upend the freshwater ecosystem, experts say. The species already has made it into the Illinois River from the Mississippi River. Fishermen contracted by the state of Illinois have removed more than 78 million pounds of invasive carp from waterways.

There have been several delays to the project, including a pause in December for another administrative review. President Donald Trump in March said "only Trump" could save the Great Lakes from Asian carp and urged governors to "join in on the fight." Those words on social media came after he met with Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer, prompting both Pritzker and Sen. Dick Durbin to demand Trump lift the review and release federal funds on the Joliet project.

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers in April instead announced that it would put Michigan officials in charge of the $1.15 billion barrier designed to keep the invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes — moving from the Rock Island district to its Detroit District.

Both sides engaged in a war of words in April, with Pritzker calling the move a “political stunt” and warning that Illinois would explore legal action if the Trump administration broke legally-binding agreements. In announcing the move, Assistant Secretary of the Army for Civil Works Adam Telle accused Illinois of being an “unreliable partner, delinquent on its payments and real estate commitments,” a claim that Pritzker denied.

The Illinois Department of Natural Resources said it first learned of the work stoppage through contractors — and followed through on a letter to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers on Thursday, with the work stoppage confirmed on July 28 after repeated attempts to reach their Detroit District.

Renee Snow, interim IDNR director, wrote in a letter to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers that she wants an “immediate” meeting to “substantiate the work stoppage and remedy project cost, schedule, and partnership impacts.”

Snow wrote that the breakdown in communication is inconsistent with procedures established under a jointly negotiated plan that guided the project.

Gary G. Perinar III, president of Carpenters Local 174 in Joliet, told the Sun-Times the project delays “not only endanger the safety of the Great Lakes but also negatively affect the working men and women who have supported this project locally.”

“This project needs to happen,” Perinar III said. “...Our members stand by eagerly awaiting the opportunity to get the job done building and strengthening our communities.”

The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers did not respond to a request for comment on Thursday.

articles.title: Gangster Uzair Baloch’s brother shot, critically injured in Karachi’s Lyari: police
articles.description: KARACHI: The brother of imprisoned Uzair Baloch , chief of the defunct People’s Amn Committee, was shot and critically wounded in Karachi’s Lyari area on Thursday evening, according to police. Chakiwara police, in a statement, said that Zubair Baloch, 40, was shot and injured on main Chakiwara Road, while two passersby were also injured. They were shifted to Civil Hospital Karachi. South Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Syed Asad Raza told Dawn that Zubair had been arrested in seven criminal cases in 2012 and was released in January 2025. He added that Zubair was sitting outside his residence in Singu Lane when armed suspects on a motorcycle opened fire on him and fled the scene. Zubair sustained multiple injuries, including to his chest and abdomen, and was undergoing surgery. DIG Raza noted that one of the injured passersby was also in serious condition. The DIG added that the police were investigating the incident from different angles, including gang rivalry and personal enmity. A social activist from the area told Dawn , on the condition of anonymity, that Zubair had joined a “political party” a few months ago and had raised its flags in his area. The activist also mentioned rumours in Lyari that some gangsters who had fled to Dubai and Iran after the Karachi operation had returned following the US-Iran war, and that residents were fearful of a possible resurgence of the past gang war in the area. They added that the attackers had covered their faces and fled when a nearby shopkeeper returned fire. Earlier in March, an anti-terrorism court (ATC) rejected bail applications of Uzair Baloch in seven cases pertaining to murder, police encounter and possession of explosives. Uzair, along with others, had been charged with attacking law enforcers with firearms and explosives in 2012 within the jurisdiction of the Kalakot police station. In April 2020, a military court had convicted Uzair Baloch of espionage and sentenced him to 12 years in jail.
